content.thinking:
I'm working out the order of the outcomes for the spec: decline, escalate, request docs, incomplete, then approve, with the ordering tied to section 2.1. I'm also weighing how the unknowns rule in section 2.2 should map to the "incomplete" outcome, since section 1 defines incomplete as a required fact not yet established.

I'm settling on an approve rule that always applies, since approve sits last in the order and anything unresolved already routes to incomplete through the unknowns rule.

I'm checking whether an approve rule with no conditions is the right fit, since it would always apply once everything above it has been ruled out. The unknowns rule means any uncertain fact sends the case to incomplete before approve is reached. I'm also noting that the 5.3 licensed-MSB exception would never take effect, because the escalate rule from 5.2 comes first in the order.

I'm checking whether section 1 needs its own approve rule, since the spec's approve outcome has to be stated somewhere. An always-true rule with no conditions fits, because the outcome order already rules out everything above it. I'm also noting that the licensed-MSB exception in 5.3 can't change any result, since the escalate rule from 5.2 is reached first.

I'm settling the approve outcome as the last rule, since anything unresolved already routes to incomplete. I'm also mapping the industry values for prohibited and msb categories, treating unlicensed money transmission as prohibited rather than as a licence-not-verified case.

I'm weighing whether the spec needs a note about industries that aren't listed, since an unmapped industry would leave the 5.1 rules unresolved and push normal businesses toward incomplete. I can't enumerate every ordinary industry, and the procedure doesn't say which ones count as normal, so I'll flag that gap as something the spec needs.

I'm now deciding which people count as identified individuals for the collections rule: the control person and anyone owning 25% or more, plus anyone the agent has already listed. I'll keep the listed flag separate from the ownership test so each person is judged on their own facts.

I'm weighing whether a listed person should count as an identified individual even when they aren't a control person or a 25% owner, since screening applies to identified individuals and a listed person could be someone of concern. I'll keep the share test on actual ownership rather than the customer's certified figure.

I'm working out how the nonprofit and excluded cases change who counts as an identified individual. Excluded entities get no identified individuals at all, and for nonprofits only the control person is identified, not the owners.

I'm weighing whether an excluded entity should have any identified individuals at all, and settling that the excluded case gets none. For the remaining entities I'll count the control person and anyone whose actual share is 25% or more, leaving out nonprofits for the ownership test, and I'll rely on the actual share rather than the customer's certified figure.

I'm settling that the excluded case gets an empty-OK rule, so when an entity is excluded, having no identified individuals counts as complete rather than unknown. For non-excluded entities with no people listed, the unknown status still stands and can route the case to incomplete.

I'm working out which individuals count as identified for the collections rule: the control person for every entity that isn't excluded, plus owners at 25% or more, with nonprofits limited to the control person. I'm also considering how to cite the SOP sections that define those two requirements.

I'm settling the collections rule: the control person counts for every entity that isn't excluded, and owners at 25% or more count only when the entity isn't a nonprofit. For excluded entities, having no identified individuals counts as complete, so the empty case is accepted there.

I'm looking at ownership completeness for section 3.3: the check is whether any unidentified person could still reach 25%, counting shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities with unknown owners. Excluded-entity shares don't belong in that total, since they're handled by the excluded rule instead.

I'm checking how excluded entities feed into the unaccounted share: an excluded holder at or above 25% needs no identification, but one below 25% still has its underlying owners unknown, so that share should count as unaccounted.

I'm checking whether an unidentified person with an actual share below 25% could still reach 25% when combined with unaccounted shares, which would make the ownership check incomplete.

I'm now checking the ownership rule for unidentified people, since a known owner below 25% could still reach 25% if they also hold some of the unaccounted shares.

I'm realizing the per-person check can't be written as a loop over unidentified people, since the collection's filter only exposes identified individuals. So I'll rely on the total of unaccounted and excluded-held shares instead, and treat that total reaching 25 as the signal for incomplete ownership.

I'm checking whether a person with a 25% or higher share needs to be identified, so the rule about identifying every such owner holds up.

I'm checking whether a known person who owns 25% or more but was never listed by the agent leaves ownership incomplete, which would call for requesting documents rather than marking the case incomplete.

I'm checking whether a known person with a share below 25% could still reach 25% once the unaccounted shares are added, since that would leave ownership incomplete. The collection filter only returns identified individuals, so I can't loop over the unidentified ones directly. I'll rely on the total of unaccounted shares instead, and I'm weighing whether a required person who was never listed by the agent should still count toward that check.

I'm wondering whether an unlisted person who is required to be identified should count against ownership completeness, or whether that case belongs under the documents request in section 3.3. I'm also considering whether the listed flag should feed into which individuals the screening rule covers.

I'm weighing whether to treat a required owner the agent never listed as a gap in ownership completeness, which would route the case to a document request. I'm leaning toward basing the requirement on the SOP rule rather than the agent's listed flag, so an unlisted owner at 25% or more still counts.

I'm checking the identification rule against the control person: the SOP wants a single control person identified, so if that field is computed as not identified for a non-excluded entity, the case should request documents. I'm also setting aside the listed flag for now, since verification of an unlisted person would catch the gap anyway.

I'm checking the control-person requirement against nonprofits too, and I'm working through the verification rule for identified individuals, where an unverified person sends the case to a document request. I'm also reading the registry-age rule in section 3.5, which I want to apply to every entity type, including excluded ones.

I'm now turning to the rules in section 4 on sanctions, PEPs, and adverse media: confirmed sanctions on the entity or any counted individual lead to decline, potential matches lead to escalation, and so do PEP flags and adverse media. I also need to note that every search has to be recorded with its terms, date, and sources, and since that record is a required fact that isn't established yet, the case can't be approved.

I'm going through the sanctions-related rules in section 6: a sanctioned country on the entity or any identified individual's residence means decline, and a high-risk country means escalate. I'm also noting the Crimea region code as something that matters for the check, then turning to the approve rule from section 1.

I'm settling on the approve rule as the final outcome, with an empty condition that always applies, since anything unresolved already routes to incomplete. I'm also wondering whether an approve rule with no conditions is acceptable, or whether the spec should state the default explicitly.

I'm settling on the approve rule as the last outcome, with no conditions beyond ruling out everything above it. I'm also mapping the industry names for prohibited and msb categories, starting with the marijuana-related business terms.

I'm writing the open-ownership computation, which adds the unaccounted shares to the excluded-entity shares below 25% to check whether ownership could still reach the threshold.

I'm working through the ownership check for section 3.3, which adds the unaccounted shares to any excluded-entity shares under 25%, and I'm planning to request documents when that total reaches the threshold for a non-excluded, non-nonprofit entity.

I'm now writing the ownership rule for section 3.3: unless the entity is excluded or a nonprofit, every owner at 25% or more gets identified, and ownership counts as complete only when the unaccounted shares can't reach 25% for anyone unidentified. I'm also setting up the control-person rule in 3.2 for the remaining entities.

I'm now writing the 3.2 control-person rule and checking whether the adverse-media search record counts as a required fact I still lack.

I'm now noting a gap for the ownership check: unidentified people with known shares need their largest share recorded, since the collection filter can't look at them directly. I'm also flagging that the SOP never says which industries count as normal, so any industry outside the prohibited, msb, and crypto lists stays unmapped and needs to be handled explicitly. Finally, I'm checking that the sanctions-potential status means a match hasn't been cleared yet, and that the "located" wording maps to residence for individuals.

I'm finishing the sections list and the approve rule's wording: the rule would read "all requirements below are met and no risk factor applies," so approve only fires once nothing above it has applied.

I'm now listing the rule identifiers I'll need: the approve rule, the control-person and ownership checks, the ID and registry-age checks, the sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screens, the industry and geography rules.

Now I'm drafting the wording for the screening rules: sanctions matches that aren't cleared yet go to escalation, and adverse media on the entity or a counted individual also goes to escalation.

I'm dropping the empty-collection pieces that some rules don't need, so the excluded-owners list stays out of the spec.

unknowns.text: A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be approved.

people.unknown_when_empty: which individuals the SOP requires to be identified (the control person and every individual owning 25% or more)
people.text: Entities on the excluded list do not require beneficial owners to be identified. ... For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. ... Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly.

computed.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share.

rules.text: all requirements below are met and no risk factor applies.

For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. If no control person is identified, request documents.

Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly. Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. ... If ownership is not complete, request documents.
Verify the identity of every identified individual. If any is unverified, request documents.
The entity's registry filing must be less than 12 months old. Otherwise request documents.
A confirmed sanctions match on the entity or any identified individual: decline.
A potential sanctions match that has not been cleared: escalate.
A politically exposed person among the identified individuals: escalate.
Adverse media on the entity or any identified individual: escalate.
Prohibited industries (marijuana-related business, adult content, unlicensed money transmission): decline.
Restricted industries (money services businesses, virtual currency): escalate.
Licensed money services businesses whose state licence has been verified may be approved.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a comprehensively sanctioned country: decline.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a FATF high-risk or increased-monitoring jurisdiction: escalate.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Approve is written as a rule that always applies, because it sits last in the order: any other rule that applies, or might apply because of an unknown fact, outranks it. 'Incomplete' is the unknowns outcome.
Sets the order: decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve.
Sets the unknowns outcome: a rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to incomplete.

An exemption, not an outcome. It is applied through the people list's counts_when (excluded entities have no identified individuals) and empty_ok_when, and through the excluded = no conditions in bo-control-person and bo-ownership-complete.
The control person also counts as an identified individual through the people list's counts_when.

The computed fact open_pct adds unaccounted shares to shares held by excluded entities below 25%. Those excluded entities' owners are unknown, and only an excluded holding of 25% or more is exempt. Owners at 25% or more count as identified individuals through counts_when.
The SOP does not say whose match counts. The rule checks the entity and the identified individuals, the same scope as 4.1.
The pack's adverse_media facts already meet the SOP's materiality and source bar. The search-record requirement is listed in needs.
'unlicensed money transmission' is mapped to prohibited through maps.industry.
Contradicts 5.3: a licensed, verified MSB is restricted, so it is escalated here. Escalate outranks approve, so industry-licensed-msb never decides a case.
Translated as written. It conflicts with 5.2 and is always outranked by it.
An individual's location is taken as their residence.
An individual's location is taken as their residence.
